column1: # Pokémon Sword on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Game Freak's engine on SDK 7.3.2, update 1.3.2 (v458752); game.tsv and the shader tables come from the survey, checked by hand. Its GFPAK archives are LZ4 (no Oodle):
# a port needs no device for the shaders. NintendoWare Vfx builds some effect programs at run time (46 in the opening, in no game file): the app captures them
# the first time it meets them (captured_shaders/) and the next port with --install translates them in; until then the draws that need them are left out, which in the
# opening showed the old shot frozen under the new one's flares and text, and an 80% dynamic-resolution frame in a corner.
# On the AYN Odin 2 (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, Adreno 740, Android 13, Turnip, 2026-11-13), driven with DM_CTL and played by hand: the language, photo and name screens (the
# overlay keyboard), the opening broadcast, the house, Postwick, door fades, the X menu, a save and Continue from it, the Odin's own controls. 30 fps as on the Switch
# (frame work about 12-14 ms); with DM_PRESENT_INTERVAL=display it renders 60 but the game steps its logic per frame and runs twice as fast, so there is no 60 fps option.
# A 15-minute soak in Postwick (devtools/soak.sh) kept one process at 33 ms a frame with no red line; the footprint settled at about 1.1 GB and crept 2-3 MiB a minute.
# With a save, the title screen crashed in 2 of 12 cold boots before patches.py (an outfit part not loaded yet); 0 of 12 with it.
# Battles, the Wild Area and local wireless are not checked yet.
